items.title: Define and implement stable task-plus-agent identity resolution
items.context: Follow Workstream D and the shipped owner-session contract. Resolution remains explicit override, validated host-adapter task+agent identity, bounded generated fallback, then warned derived-ppid fallback. Do not use a repository-global token or collapse reviewer and implementer privileges.
items.userSees: User sees "owner session: <stable-id> [host-adapter]" remain unchanged across same-task shell boundaries; a different task or role sees the existing foreign-owner rejection.

items.title: Propagate stable identity through supported host adapters and diagnostics
items.context: Codex, Claude, and agy adapter paths must retain task and agent/role identity across child shells without exposing raw host tokens. session_brief and mutation warnings must report the identity source and degraded derived-ppid fallback.
items.userSees: User sees "session identity degraded: derived-ppid" with an actionable LATTICE_SESSION_ID/adapter hint before the first owner-gated mutation; supported adapters report their provider and source without raw tokens.

items.title: Prove isolation, compatibility, and takeover behavior with bounded regressions
items.context: Cover same task/agent across PPID changes, different tasks in one repository, implementer versus reviewer separation, explicit override, genuine foreign lease blocking, stale/active takeover, degraded warning, and supported adapter cases without live-host dependence where deterministic seams suffice.
items.userSees: User sees the same established stale/active takeover guidance for a genuine foreign lease, while same-task shell changes proceed without "foreign owner".

adversarial.desc: With deterministic resolver inputs holding project/worktree, taskIdentity, agentOrRoleIdentity, and adapter session boundary constant while shell and ppid values change, every invocation resolves the same opaque owner id and refreshes the existing lease without a foreign-owner rejection; the test must fail if ppid leaks into a validated task-plus-agent identity.

With the same repository, worktree, provider, and agent identity but two independent task identities, deterministic adapter/generated-token seams resolve different owner ids; each task can own its own story, and neither task can inherit or refresh the other task owner lease through a repository-global or thread-only token.

Within one task/thread, implementer, verification-intent, reviewer, and delivery agent/role inputs resolve distinct identities unless an explicit canonical shared-ownership policy fixture says otherwise; reviewer or intent identity cannot refresh, seize, or count as the implementer owner merely because provider, task, thread, worktree, or parent process matches.

A trimmed non-empty explicit LATTICE_SESSION_ID deterministically wins conflicting adapter, generated-token, and ppid inputs across parent changes, while a blank/whitespace override is ignored; diagnostics identify explicit-env without exposing raw native host tokens or promoting the override to authentication/reviewer/Authority proof.

For an active lease owned by a genuinely different resolved task-plus-agent session, every ordinary story-scoped mutation fails closed and preserves the established error facts: story, owner id/cwd/heartbeat, ACTIVE verdict, current session, and read-only/wait/--forceTakeover guidance; same-worktree proximity must not bypass the block.

Identity stabilization does not change takeover semantics: a stale foreign lease transfers only with explicit --takeover and an auditable event; an active foreign lease rejects ordinary mutation and --takeover, transferring only through deliberate --forceTakeover or the canonical human-approved path, with ownership and heartbeat updated atomically.

When explicit env, validated adapter identity, and generated-token seams are all absent, deterministic hostname/root/ppid inputs use derived-ppid only: changing ppid changes the id, session_brief/doctor label the source degraded, and an actionable export-LATTICE_SESSION_ID/use-supported-adapter warning appears before the first owner-gated mutation rather than falsely treating shell changes as one session.

Table-driven deterministic seams for Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, Antigravity, and agy prove that each adapter maps stable task plus agent/role inputs to the canonical resolver across ppid changes, separates changed task/role/session-boundary inputs, preserves provider as diagnostics only, redacts raw host tokens, and requires no live-host call or provider-specific branch in generic lease logic.

For a supported adapter without a native stable signal, generated-token fixtures reuse one opaque id only within the same project, provider, task, agent/role, and adapter session boundary; changing any isolation dimension does not collide, persisted state follows registered runtime-artifact cleanup/material-hygiene rules, and raw tokens never enter story evidence or logs.

Legacy readable lease source labels are normalized through the canonical resolver without changing the stored owner identity, granting role/task privilege, or bypassing foreign-owner checks; active/stale classification and takeover guidance remain identical for a legacy lease fixture and its canonical equivalent.

items.title: Ratify the canonical task-and-agent identity contract before runtime implementation
items.context: Before any runtime code change, record understanding and a structured decision with at least three adversarial pre-mortem scenarios, explicitly update or confirm the canonical owner-session identity contract, and obtain fresh review evidence from at least two independent real hosts as required by Workstream D. This decision must settle task identity, role separation, resolution priority, fallback storage/cleanup, observability, and non-goals.
items.userSees: User sees "two-host owner-session contract review: PASS (codex + antigravity; local assurance only)" before runtime implementation begins.
excludes: No runtime owner-session implementation begins before the decision and independent-host review evidence are accepted.
